bmt-2020-geometry-02.title: Quadratic in the radius
bmt-2020-geometry-02.body:
Let the radii be $r_1,r_2$. Because $O_1$ and $O_2$ have centers on $AB$, are tangent to each other and to $O$ at its ends, their diameters together fill $AB$: $2r_1+2r_2=2$, so $r_1+r_2=1$.

The total area is $\pi(r_1^2+r_2^2)=\pi\left(r_1^2+(1-r_1)^2\right)=\pi(2r_1^2-2r_1+1)$, minimized at $r_1=\tfrac12$ with value $\tfrac\pi2$. So $m+n=3$.

**Answer: 3**

bmt-2020-geometry-02.title: QM-AM
bmt-2020-geometry-02.body:
$r_1^2+r_2^2\ge\frac{(r_1+r_2)^2}2=\frac12$, with equality when $r_1=r_2=\tfrac12$, so the minimum area is $\tfrac\pi2$ and $m+n=3$.

**Answer: 3**

bmt-2020-geometry-03.title: Base times height
bmt-2020-geometry-03.body:
The lateral edges are perpendicular to the base, so $BE\perp AB$ and triangle $ABE$ is right-angled at $B$ with $\angle EAB=60^\circ$ and hypotenuse $AE=2$: $AB=2\cos60^\circ=1$ and the height is $BE=2\sin60^\circ=\sqrt3$.

In the base, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, $\angle CAB=60^\circ$ and $AB=1$, so $BC=\tan60^\circ=\sqrt3$ and the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $\tfrac12\cdot1\cdot\sqrt3=\tfrac{\sqrt3}2$.

Volume $=\tfrac{\sqrt3}2\cdot\sqrt3=\tfrac32$, so $m+n=5$.

**Answer: 5**

bmt-2020-geometry-05.title: Geometric series of nested squares
bmt-2020-geometry-05.body:
Each $A_iB_iC_iD_i$ is a square, and each square sits inside the previous one in the same way, so $[A_iB_iC_iD_i]=k\,[A_{i-1}B_{i-1}C_{i-1}D_{i-1}]$ for a constant $k$.

$A_2$ lies on $A_1B_1$ with $A_1A_2=\tfrac{2019}{2020}$ and $D_2$ lies on $D_1A_1$ with $A_1D_2=\tfrac1{2020}$. The square $A_1B_1C_1D_1$ is the square $A_2B_2C_2D_2$ plus four congruent right triangles like $A_1A_2D_2$, each of area $\tfrac12\cdot\tfrac{2019}{2020}\cdot\tfrac1{2020}$. So
$$k=1-\frac{4\cdot2019}{2\cdot2020^2}=1-\frac{2019}{2\cdot1010^2}.$$
The sum is $\dfrac{1}{1-k}=\dfrac{2\cdot1010^2}{2019}=\dfrac{1010^2\cdot2}{2019}$. Here $2019=3\cdot673$ is coprime to $2\cdot1010^2$, so with $b=2$ squarefree, $a=1010$, $c=2019$ (smallest possible).

$a+b+c=1010+2+2019=3031$.

**Answer: 3031**

bmt-2020-geometry-06.title: Embed in a box
bmt-2020-geometry-06.body:
A tetrahedron whose four faces are congruent is a disphenoid: it is inscribed in a rectangular box with edge lengths $x,y,z$ so that the tetrahedron's six edges are face diagonals of the box. Its opposite edges are equal, so the three edge lengths $5,5,6$ satisfy
$$x^2+y^2=25,\quad y^2+z^2=25,\quad z^2+x^2=36.$$
Adding: $x^2+y^2+z^2=43$, so $z^2=18$, $x^2=18$, $y^2=7$.

The tetrahedron's volume is one third of the box's: $V=\tfrac13xyz$, so
$$V^2=\frac{x^2y^2z^2}{9}=\frac{18\cdot7\cdot18}{9}=252.$$

**Answer: 252**

bmt-2020-geometry-08.title: Symmedians and mass points
bmt-2020-geometry-08.body:
Reflecting a median over the angle bisector gives the symmedian, so $AD$, $BE$, $CF$ are symmedians and $K$ is the symmedian (Lemoine) point. Since $\angle BAD=\angle CAM_A$ and $\angle DAC=\angle BAM_A$,
$$\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{[ABD]}{[ADC]}=\frac{AB\sin\angle BAD}{AC\sin\angle DAC}=\frac{AB\sin\angle CAM_A}{AC\sin\angle BAM_A}.$$
Because $M_A$ is the midpoint of $BC$, $[ABM_A]=[ACM_A]$, i.e. $AB\sin\angle BAM_A=AC\sin\angle CAM_A$, so $\frac{\sin\angle CAM_A}{\sin\angle BAM_A}=\frac{AB}{AC}$ and $\frac{BD}{DC}=\left(\frac{AB}{AC}\right)^2$. Similarly $\frac{CE}{EA}=\left(\frac{BC}{BA}\right)^2$ and $\frac{AF}{FB}=\left(\frac{CA}{CB}\right)^2$.

Assign masses $A:BC^2$, $B:CA^2$, $C:AB^2$. Then $F$ carries mass $BC^2+CA^2$ and the total mass at $K$ is $a^2+b^2+c^2$ (with $a=BC$, $b=CA$, $c=AB$). Since $\frac{[KAB]}{[CAB]}=\frac{KF}{CF}=\frac{\text{mass}(C)}{\text{total mass}}$ (and similarly for the others),
$$[KAB]:[KBC]:[KCA]=c^2:a^2:b^2=17^2:14^2:12^2=289:196:144.$$
These three numbers have no common factor, so $p+q+r=289+196+144=629$.

**Answer: 629**

bmt-2020-geometry-09.title: Reduce to a triangle with sides $1,p,p$
bmt-2020-geometry-09.body:
The minimum is attained by a degenerate polygon that is really a triangle (several of the given segments lie end to end on one straight side).

**Step 1: a minimal polygon has only three genuine corners.** Suppose four genuine corners form a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ with sides $a,b,c,d$. By Bretschneider's formula its area is $\sqrt{(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)(s-d)-abcd\cos^2\frac{B+D}2}$. With the side lengths fixed, deforming the quadrilateral to increase $\angle B+\angle D$ (keeping all angles $\le180^\circ$) makes $\cos^2\frac{B+D}2$ larger and so decreases the area. Hence such a polygon is not minimal, and a minimizer has exactly three genuine corners, i.e. it is a triangle whose sides are sums of some of the $F_i$.

**Step 2: among integer-sided triangles with perimeter $2p+1$, the minimal area is that of the triangle $1,p,p$.** Take sides $a\le b\le c$ with $a>1$. Replacing $(a,b)$ by $(a-1,b+1)$ keeps the perimeter and changes $(s-a)(s-b)$ to $(s-a)(s-b)+a-b-1<(s-a)(s-b)$, so the area decreases (the triangle inequality still holds). So the minimum has $a=1$ and then $b=c=p$.

**Step 3: it can be achieved.** The perimeter is $F_1+\cdots+F_{2020}=F_{2022}-1$, odd because $F_{2022}$ is even ($3\mid2022$). Let $p=\frac{F_{2022}-2}2$. Take one side $F_1=1$. Since $F_{3n-1}+F_{3n}=F_{3n+1}$, the sum of all the $F_{3n+1}$ ($n\ge1$) equals the sum of all the remaining terms $F_2,F_3,F_5,F_6,\dots$, and each equals $p$. So the segments can be laid out as a triangle with sides $1,p,p$.

**Area.** The altitude to the side $1$ is $\sqrt{p^2-\frac14}$, so the area is $\frac12\sqrt{p^2-\frac14}=\frac{\sqrt{4p^2-1}}4=\frac{\sqrt{(F_{2022}-2)^2-1}}4$.

This matches the form with $(a,b,c,d)=(2022,2,1,4)$, giving $a+b+c+d=2029$.

**Answer: 2029**

bmt-2020-geometry-10.title: Urquhart's theorem
bmt-2020-geometry-10.body:
The foci are $2\sqrt{13^2-12^2}=10$ apart, and $RA+AS=26$ with $RA=AS$ gives $RA=AS=13$.

**Urquhart's theorem.** In this configuration $RP+PS=RQ+QS$ (equivalently $P$ and $Q$ lie on a common ellipse with foci $R,S$; by Pitot's theorem this follows from the existence of a circle tangent to the four lines $RP,PS,SQ,QR$). Hence the perimeter of $RPSQ$ is $2(RP+PS)$.

Place $R=(-5,0)$, $S=(5,0)$; then $A=(0,12)$ since $RA=AS=13$. $P$ lies on ray $RA$ beyond $A$ with $AP=26$, so $RP=13+26=39$ and $P=R+3(A-R)=(10,36)$. Then $PS=\sqrt{5^2+36^2}=\sqrt{1321}$.

The perimeter is $2(39+\sqrt{1321})=78+\sqrt{5284}$, so $m=78$, $n=5284$ and $m+n=5362$. (Constructing $B$ and $Q$ numerically confirms $RQ+QS=RP+PS\approx75.35$.)

**Answer: 5362**
